about: The iPhone app's performance budgets, held by PerfTests.swift on a simulator against a dev node with a busy fleet (scripts/dev-node.ts --heavy --auto-approve). A number over its limit fails the test. Where the X2 study's target (26 November 2026) is not met yet, the limit holds what was measured from getting worse, and the target is checked too, its miss recorded in every run as an expected failure until it is met. Launch is held from the app's own first line to Home's first frame with what it shows: before that is the platform's (on a simulator the process and its loader, and the libraries XCUITest and a device panel's tooling put into the app: 1.5–3.5 s measured), which the suite reports but can't hold the app to. Measured 26 November 2026, iOS 27.0 simulator, Debug (I9): the app's own launch 0.83–1.0 s under XCUITest (0.42–0.45 s launched plainly), CPU at rest 0.0–3.7 % over three runs, 8.8 ms a second of late frames scrolling. Measured again the same day on CI's Mac, the mini's iOS 27.2 simulator, Debug (I10), the app's first line now before it reads its key and its kept agents: its own launch 0.52 s under XCUITest when the Mac was quiet and up to 1.01 s when it wasn't (0.27–0.54 s launched plainly), something needing you on screen in 0.16–0.21 s at the 95th percentile, a dead link back in 0.94–1.02 s, 40–43 MB and 0.1 % of a core at rest. So three limits were tightened, each with room for a busy CI Mac: the event to 0.5 s, back to 1.5 s, memory to 80 MB. Launch keeps 1.5 s (a busy Mac doubles it), CPU at rest 5 % (I9 saw 3.7 % once), requests at rest X2's 2, a dead link noticed 5 s (three of the node's beats are 4.5 s), and scrolling 15 ms a second on the best of its three rounds (as measured since 26 November). Change a limit only on purpose, in its own reviewed change, saying why.
